\label{lem:ra-stab-gen-vi}
Let $g(z;x) = g_1(z;x) + g_2(z)$ such that $g_1:\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}\times\ensuremath{\mathcal{X}}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^d$ is $L$-bounded and $\beta$-Lipschitz with respect to $z$ and $g_2:\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^d$ is any (data indepedent) operator. 
Let $z^*\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}$ be its population equilibrium point. For any $x\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{X}}$, define $h(z;x)=\left\langle g(z;x),z-z^* \right\rangle$. For $S\sim \mathcal{D}^n$, let $H_S(z) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{x\in S} h(z;x)$ and $H_\mathcal{D}(z) = \underset{x\sim\mathcal{D}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ h(z;x) \right]$. Then for any $\Delta$-UAS algorithm, $\mathcal{A}$, one has
$\underset{S,A}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}(S))-H_S(\mathcal{A}(S)) \right] \leq \Delta(\betaB+L)$.

label: fact:grad-dual-relation
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:grad-dual-relation}
For any $z$, it holds that $\|\nabla (\frac{1}{2}\|z\|^2)\|_* \leq \|z\|$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the chain rule we have 
$\nabla (\frac{1}{2}\|z\|^2) = \|z\|\cdot \nabla(\|z\|)$ 
and so 
$\|\nabla (\frac{1}{2}\|z\|^2)\|_* = \|z\|\cdot \|\nabla(\|z\|)\|_*$. 
Thus, it only remains to show that $\|\nabla(\|z\|)\|_* \leq 1$.
By the definition of the dual norm we have $\|\nabla(\|z\|)\|_* = \max\limits_{v:\|v\|\leq1}\left\{{\left\langle \nabla(\|z\|),v \right\rangle}\right\}$. Further, by the definition of the subgradient we have for any $z'$ that 
$\|z'\| - \|z\| \geq \left\langle \nabla(\|z\|),z'-z \right\rangle$.
Substituting $v=z'-z$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \left\langle \nabla(\|z\|),v \right\rangle \leq \|v+z\|-\|z\| 
    \leq \|v\| + \|z\| - \|z\| = \|v\| \leq 1,
\end{align*}
as desired.

label: lem:sc-op-stability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sc-op-stability}
Let $\mu,\lambda > 0$ and $\rho$ be $\mu$-strongly monotone w.r.t. $\|\cdot\|$. Then for any point $z_0\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}$, the algorithm which outputs the unique equilibrium of $G_S(z) + \frac{\lambda}{\mu} (\rho(z)-\rho(z_0))$ is $\big(\frac{2L}{\mu \lambda n}\big)$-uniform argument stable w.r.t. $S$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $z_\lambda$ and $z_\lambda'$ denote the equilibrium points of the regularized operators w.r.t. to adjacent datasets $S$ and $S'$ respectively.
By the equilibrium condition we have for any $z\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}$
\begin{align*}
    \left\langle G_S(z_\lambda) + \lambda[\rho(z_\lambda) - \rho(z_0)],z-z_\lambda \right\rangle &\geq 0 \\
    \left\langle G_{S'}(z_\lambda') + \lambda[\rho(z_\lambda') - \rho(z_0)],z-z_\lambda' \right\rangle &\geq 0 \\
    \implies \left\langle G_S(z_\lambda) - G_{S'}(z_\lambda') + \lambda[\rho(z_\lambda) - \rho(z_\lambda')],z_\lambda' - z_\lambda \right\rangle &\geq 0.
\end{align*}
Since $\rho$ is a $1$-strongly monotone operator we have
\begin{align*}
    \left\langle G_S(z_\lambda) - G_{S'}(z_\lambda'),z_\lambda' - z_\lambda \right\rangle &\geq \lambda \left\langle \rho(z_\lambda) - \rho(z_\lambda'),z_\lambda - z_\lambda' \right\rangle \geq \mu\lambda \|z_\lambda - z_\lambda'\|^2.
\end{align*}
Now we can use the monotonicity of $G$ to derive,
\begin{align*}
    \mu\lambda \|z_\lambda - z_\lambda'\|^2 &\leq \left\langle G_S(z_\lambda) - G_{S'}(z_\lambda'),z_\lambda' - z_\lambda \right\rangle \\
    &= \left\langle G_S(z_\lambda) - G_{S'}(z_\lambda),z_\lambda' - z_\lambda \right\rangle + \left\langle G_{S'}(z_\lambda) - G_{S'}(z_\lambda'),z_\lambda' - z_\lambda \right\rangle \\
    &\overset{(i)}{\leq} \left\langle G_S(z_\lambda) - G_{S'}(z_\lambda),z_\lambda' - z_\lambda \right\rangle \\
    &\overset{(ii)}{\leq} \|G_{S}(z_\lambda) - G_{S'}(z_\lambda)\|_\ast\cdot\|z_\lambda' - z_\lambda\| \\
    &\overset{(iii)}{\leq} \frac{2L}{n}\|z_\lambda' - z_\lambda\|.
\end{align*}
Above $(i)$ comes from the monotonicity of $G$, step $(ii)$ comes from H\"older's inequality, and step $(iii)$ comes from the fact that $S$ and $S'$ differ in at most one point.
Simple algebra now obtains $\|z_\lambda-z_\lambda'\| \leq \frac{2L}{\mu \lambda n}$.

label: fact:vi-gap-doesnt-bound-sp-gap
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fact:vi-gap-doesnt-bound-sp-gap}
There exists a differentiable convex-concave loss, distribution $\mathcal{D}$, and point $z'$ such that when the operator is the saddle operator of the loss, $\operatorname{VI-Gap}(z) < \operatorname{Gap_{\mathsf{SP}}}(z)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We show that the VI-gap is upper bounded by the excess risk of some convex function with operator $g(z)=\nabla f(z)$. Since stochastic convex optimization is a special case of SSPs, this shows there exist scenarios where $\operatorname{Gap_{\mathsf{SP}}} \nleq \operatorname{VI-Gap}$. Specifically, when the dual player space $\Theta$ is singleton, the SP-gap becomes the excess risk.

Let $f(z;x)=z^2$ be defined over $z\in[0,1]$, and so it does not matter what the distribution or data domain is. Note that $\operatorname{VI-Gap}$ becomes
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{VI-Gap}(z) = \max_{u\in[0,1]}\left\{{\left\langle \nabla f(u),z-u \right\rangle}\right\} = \max_{u\in[0,1]}\left\{{2uz - 2u^2}\right\}.
\end{align*}
Note that in this case the SP-gap is just the excess risk, $\operatorname{Gap_{\mathsf{SP}}}(z)=z^2-\min_{z\in[0,1]}\left\{{z^2}\right\}=z^2$. 

Consider the point $z=1$. It is easy to show that $\operatorname{VI-Gap}(1)=0.5$ but $\operatorname{Gap_{\mathsf{SP}}}(1)=1$, proving the claim.
head: environment

label: lem:ra-stab-gen-2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ra-stab-gen-2} (Restatement of Lemma \ref{lem:ra-stab-gen})
Let $f:\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}\times\ensuremath{\mathcal{X}}\mapsto \mathbb{R}$ be $L$-Lipschitz. Let $[w^*,\theta^*]\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}$ be the population saddle point. For any $x\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{X}}$ define $h([w,\theta];x)=f(w,\theta^*;x) - f(w^*,\theta;x)$. For $S\sim \mathcal{D}^n$, let $H_S(z) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{x\in S} h(z;x)$ and $H_\mathcal{D}(z) = \underset{x\sim\mathcal{D}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ h(z;x) \right]$. Then for any $\Delta$-UAS algorithm, $\mathcal{A}$, one has
$\underset{S,A}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{A}(S))-H_S(\mathcal{A}(S)) \right] \leq 2\Delta L$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This result follows simply from two facts. First, because $f$ is an $L$-Lipschitz function for any $x\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{X}}$, we can show that $h$ is $L$-Lipschitz. For any $[w,\theta],[w',\theta']\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}$ observe,
\begin{align*}
    h([w,\theta]) - h([w',\theta']) &= [f(w,\theta^*;x)-f(w^*,\theta;x)] - [f(w',\theta^*;x)-f(w^*,\theta';x)] \\
    &= f(w,\theta^*;x) - f(w',\theta^*;x) + f(w^*,\theta';x) - f(w^*,\theta;x) \\
    &\leq 2L\|[w,\theta]-[w',\theta']\|.
\end{align*}

The rest of the proof essentially follows from the stability implies generalization proof of \cite{bousquet2002stability} since $H_\mathcal{D}$ and $H_S$ have a statistical form w.r.t. $h$. In more detail, for any $i\in[n]$ denote $S^{(i)}$ as the dataset which replaces the $i$'th datapoint of $S$, $x_i$, with a fresh sample from $\mathcal{D}$, $x'$. We have the following: 
\begin{align*}
    \underset{S,\mathcal{A}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_{\mathcal{D}}(\mathcal{A}(S)) - H_S(\mathcal{A}(S)) \right] 
    &= \underset{S,\mathcal{A}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \underset{x}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ h(\mathcal{A}(S);x) \right] - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{x\in S}[h(\mathcal{A}(S);x)] \right] \\
    &= \underset{S,x'\sim\mathcal{D}^{n+1},i\sim\mathsf{Unif}([n])}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ h(\mathcal{A}(S^{(i)});x_i) - h(\mathcal{A}(S);x_i) \right] \\
    &= \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ h(\mathcal{A}(S^{(i)};x_i) - h(\mathcal{A}(S);x_i) \right] \\
    &\leq \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ L\|\mathcal{A}(S^{(i)}) - \mathcal{A}(S)\| \right] \leq 2L\Delta.
\end{align*}
The last step follows from the previously established Lipschitzness property of $h$.

label: lem:moment-accountant
title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $\epsilon,\delta \in (0,1]$ and $c$ be a universal constant. Let $D\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Y}}^n$ be a dataset over some domain $\ensuremath{\mathcal{Y}}$, and let $h_1,...,h_T:\ensuremath{\mathcal{Y}}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^d$ be a series of (possibly adaptive) queries such that for any $y\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Y}}$, $t\in[T]$,  $\left\|h_t(y)\right\|_2 \leq L$. Let $\sigma \geq \frac{c L \sqrt{T\log(1/\delta)}}{n\epsilon}$ and 
$T \geq \frac{n^2\epsilon}{b^2}$.
Then the algorithm which samples batches of size $B_1,..,B_t$ of size $b$ uniformly at random and outputs $\frac{1}{b}\sum_{y\in B_t}h_t(y) + g_t$ for all $t\in[T]$ where $g_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\mathbb{I}_d\sigma^2)$, is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-DP.
head: environment

label: thm:noisy-mirror-prox
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L = B_2^2L_w^2 + B_\theta^2L_\theta^2$ and let $p^*=\frac{\bar{p}}{\bar{p}-1}$ and $q^*=\frac{\bar{q}}{\bar{q}-1}$ be the conjugate exponents of $\bar p$ and $\bar q$, respectively. For $t\in[T]$ denote the result of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}(z_t)$ as $[\nabla_{w,t},\nabla_{\theta,t}]$ such that $\nabla_{w,t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_w}$ and $\nabla_{\theta,t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_\theta}$.

We consider the following construction of the private operator oracle, $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}$, for $G_S$. Our implementation adds Gaussian noise to minibatch estimates of $G_S$. That is, to evaluate $\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}(z_t)$, we uniformly sample a minibatch of size $m=\max\left\{{n\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon}{T}},1}\right\}$, call it $M_t$, as well as Gaussian noise vectors $\xi_{w,t} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\mathbb{I}_{d_w} \sigma_w^2)$ and $\xi_{\theta,t} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\mathbb{I}_{d_\theta} \sigma_\theta^2)$, for some $\sigma_w,\sigma_\theta >0$. We then have that 
\begin{align*}
    [\nabla_{w,t},\nabla_{\theta,t}] = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{x\in M_t} g(w_t,\theta_t;x) + [\xi_{w,t},\xi_{\theta,t}].
\end{align*}

\textit{Privacy Bound:} We first bound the privacy of Algorithm \ref{alg:mirror-prox}. Since for any $u$, $\|u\|_{2} \leq \sqrt{d^{1-{2/p^*}}}\|u\|_{p*}$, we can bound the privacy loss using the guarantees of the moments accountant, Lemma \ref{lem:moment-accountant}. 
Specifically, we set  $T = \kappa\min\left\{{n,\frac{n^2\epsilon^2}{d\log(1/\delta)\tilde{\kappa}}}\right\}$, $\eta=\frac{\hat{D}}{L\sqrt{T}}$, use minibatches of size $m=\max\left\{{n\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon}{T}},1}\right\}$, and set $\sigma_w = \frac{cB_wL_w\sqrt{T d_w^{1-2/p^*}\log(1/\delta)}}{n\epsilon}$ and $\sigma_\theta = \frac{cB_\thetaL_\theta\sqrt{T d_\theta^{1-2/p^*}\log(1/\delta)}}{n\epsilon}$ for some universal constant $c$. It can be verified this scale of noise satisfies the conditions of Lemma \ref{lem:moment-accountant} and thus ensures $(\epsilon,\delta)$-DP.

\textit{Utility Bound:} We now establish the convergence guarantee by applying the general convergence guarantee of stochastic mirror prox (Lemma \ref{lem:mirror-prox-bound}, Appendix \ref{app:mirror-prox}) with $\psi([w,\theta]) = \frac{\kappa}{2B_w^2}\|w\|_{\bar p}^2 + \frac{\kappa}{2B_\theta^2}\|\theta\|_{\bar q}^2$, which is $1$-strongly convex w.r.t. $\|\cdot\|$. Clearly our saddle operator oracle yields unbiased estimates of $G_S(z)$ at each iteration. 
To bound the variance, $\tau$, note when $p\neq 2$ the private estimate of $\nabla_{w,t}$ satisfies
$$\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\nabla_{w,t} - \nabla_w F_S(w_t,\theta_t)\|_{p^*}^2 \right] 
\overset{(i)}{\leq} d_w^{2/p^*}\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\xi_{w,t}\|_{\infty}^2 \right] 
\leq d_w^{2/p^*}\sigma_{w}^2\log(d) \leq \frac{c^2B_w^2L_w^2T d_w\log(1/\delta)\log(d)}{n^2\epsilon^2}.$$
When $p=2$, then $p^*=2$, and one can replace bound $(i)$ with $\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\xi_{w,t}\|_{2}^2 \right]$. Combining these cases yields a bound of $\big(\frac{c^2B_w^2L_w^2T d_w\log(1/\delta)\tilde{\kappa}}{n^2\epsilon^2}\Big)$ on the variance of $\nabla_{w,t}$.
A similar analysis holds for $\nabla_{\theta,t}$.
Ultimately, with respect to the norm chosen above, we get $\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}(z_t) - G(z_t)\|_*^2 \right] \leq \tau^2$ with
\begin{align*}
    \tau^2 \leq (B_w^2L_w^2 + B_\theta^2L_\theta^2)\left({1+\frac{c^2Td\log(1/\delta)\tilde{\kappa}}{n^2\epsilon^2}}\right) = O(L^2\kappa).
\end{align*}
The last equality uses the fact that $\kappa \geq 1$.
Recall we choose $\psi([w,\theta]) = \frac{\kappa}{2B_w^2}\|w\|_{\bar p}^2 + \frac{\kappa}{2B_\theta^2}\|\theta\|_{\bar q}^2$, 
and thus
$\psi([w,\theta]) = \kappa\|[w,\theta]\|^2$.
Now the guarantees of Lemma \ref{lem:mirror-prox-bound} imply
\begin{align*}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\langle G_S(z_{t^*}),z_{t^*}-z \right\rangle \right] = \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}(z_t),z_t-z \right\rangle \right] = O\left({\frac{\kappa \hat{D}^2}{T\eta} + \frac{7\eta}{2}(L^2 + 2\tau^2)}\right).
\end{align*}
The theorem statement now follows from plugging in the parameter settings of $T$ and $\eta$ and the bound on $\tau$ established above.

For any $z_1,z_2\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}$ we have
\begin{align*}
    \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(z_1) - \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(z_2) &= \max_{z}\left\{{\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}(z),z_1-z \right\rangle}\right\} - \max_{z'}\left\{{\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}(z'),z_2-z' \right\rangle}\right\} \\
    &\leq \max_{z}\left\{{\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}(z),z_1-z \right\rangle - \left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}(z),z_1-z \right\rangle}\right\} \\
    &= \max_{z}\left\{{\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}(z),z_1-z_2 \right\rangle}\right\} \\
    &\leq \|G_{\mathcal{D}}(z)\|_*\|z_1-z_2\| \leq L\|z_1-z_2\|.
\end{align*}

title: Proof
body_md:
We will prove both properties via induction on $B_1,...,B_T$. Specifically, for each $t\in[T]$ we will introduce two terms $E_t$ and $F_t$, and show that 
these terms are bounded 
if the bound on $B_{t}$ holds and that $B_t$ holds if
$E_{t-1}$ and $F_{t-1}$ are bounded. 
Property \ref{prop:p1-vi} is then established as a result of the fact that $\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z_{t}^*\right\|^2 \right] \leq 2(E_t+F_t)$.
Note that $B_1$ holds as the base case because 
$\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|z_{1}^* - z_0^*\right\|^2 \right] \leq B^2$.

\paragraph{Property \ref{prop:p1-vi}:} 
We here prove that if $B_t$ is sufficiently bounded, then $E_t$ and $F_t$ are bounded where 
for $t\in [T]$ we define
\begin{align} \label{eq:EF-vi}
    E_t = \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z^*_{S,t}\right\|^2 \right],
    && F_t = \frac{\kappa}{2^t\lambda}\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_\mathcal{D}^{(t)}\left({z^*_{S,t}}\right) \right].
\end{align}
Additionally, this will establish property \ref{prop:p1-vi} because for any $t\in[T]$ it holds that, 
\begin{align}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z_{t}^*\right\|^2 \right] \nonumber 
    &\leq  2\Bigg(\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z^*_{S,t}\right\|^2 \right] + \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|z^*_{S,t} - z^*_{t}\right\|^2 \right]\Bigg) \nonumber \\
    &\leq  2\Bigg(\underbrace{\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z^*_{S,t}\right\|^2 \right]}_{E_t} + \underbrace{\frac{\kappa}{2^t\lambda}\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_\mathcal{D}^{(t)}\left({z^*_{S,t}}\right) \right]}_{F_t}\Bigg). \label{eq:E-F-G-vi}
\end{align}
The second inequality comes from the strong monotonicity of the operator (see Fact \ref{fact:rel-acc-bounds-distance-vi}). 

Since $E_t$ is bounded by the assumption made in the statement of Theorem \ref{thm:vi-generalized-rr-convergence}, we focus on bounding $F_t$.
We have 
\begin{align*}
    \frac{\kappa}{2^t\lambda}\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_\mathcal{D}^{(t)}\left({z^*_{S,t}}\right) \right]
    &= \frac{\kappa}{2^t\lambda}\,\,\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_\mathcal{D}^{(t)}\left({z^*_{S,t}}\right) \Big| \mathcal{F}_{t-1} \right] \right] \\
    &\leq  \frac{\kappa}{2^{t}\lambda}\Big(\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ H_S^{(t)}\left({z^*_{S,t}}\right)\Big| \mathcal{F}_{t-1} \right] \right]+\frac{\kappa\tilde{L}^2}{2^t\lambda n'}\Big) \\
    &= \frac{\kappa}{2^{t}\lambda}\Big(\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\langle G_S^{(t)}(z_{S,t}^*),z_{S,t}^*-z^*_t \right\rangle\Big| \mathcal{F}_{t-1} \right] \right]+\frac{\kappa\tilde{L}^2}{2^t\lambda n'}\Big) \\
    &\leq \frac{\kappa^2\tilde{L}^2}{2^{2t}\lambda^2 n'} 
    \leq \frac{B^2}{2304 \cdot 2^{2t}\kappa^2}. 
\end{align*}
The first inequality comes from the fact that stability implies generalization for $H^{(t)}$, Lemma \ref{lem:ra-stab-gen-vi}. Note the algorithm which outputs this exact equilibrium point is $\frac{L}{2^t\lambda n'}$ uniform argument stable (see Lemma \ref{lem:sc-op-stability}/Assumption \ref{assm:operator}).
The second inequality comes from the fact that $z^*_{S,t}$ is the exact empirical equilibrium point of the regularized objective, and so for any $z\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}$, $\left\langle G_S^{(t)}(z_{S,t}^*),z_{S,t}^*-z \right\rangle \leq 0$. The final inequality uses the setting of $\lambda$.

We thus have a final bound $2(E_t + F_t) \leq \frac{B^2}{2^{2t}}$.

\paragraph{Property \ref{prop:p2-vi}:}
Now assume $B_{t-1}$ holds. 
We have 
     
                   
       
             
                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                            
                                 
                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                       
                        
                                     
                   
              
                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                             
                                                   
             
 
\begin{align*}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|z^*_{t} - z^*_{t-1}\right\|^2 \right] 
    &\leq \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \frac{\kappa}{2^t \lambda}\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(t)}(z^*_{t-1}),z^*_{t-1}-z_t^* \right\rangle \right] \\
    &= \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \frac{\kappa}{2^t \lambda}\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(t-1)}(z^*_{t-1}) + 2^t\lambda\rho(z^*_{t-1}-\bar{z}_{t-1}),z^*_{t-1}-z_t^* \right\rangle \right] \\
    &= \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \frac{\kappa}{2^t \lambda}\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(t-1)}(z^*_{t-1}),z^*_{t-1}-z_t^* \right\rangle + \kappa\left\langle \rho(z^*_{t-1}-\bar{z}_{t-1}),z^*_{t-1}-z_t^* \right\rangle \right] \\
    &\overset{(i)}{\leq} \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \frac{\kappa^2}{2}\|\rho(z^*_{t-1}-\bar{z}_{t-1})\|_*^2 + \frac{1}{2}\|z^*_{t-1}-z^*_t\|^2 \right] \\
    &\overset{(ii)}{\leq} \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \frac{\kappa^2}{2}\|z^*_{t-1}-\bar{z}_{t-1}\|^2 + \frac{1}{2}\|z^*_{t-1}-z^*_t\|^2 \right]. \\
\end{align*} 
Inequality $(i)$ above comes from Young's inequality and the fact that $z^*_{t-1}$ is the equilibrium point w.r.t. $G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(t-1)}$. Inequality $(ii)$ comes from Fact \ref{fact:grad-dual-relation}/Assumption \ref{assm:operator}. After re-arranging we can continue as follows:
\begin{align*}
 \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|z^*_{t} - z^*_{t-1}\right\|^2 \right] \leq \kappa^2\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|z^*_{t-1}-\bar{z}_{t-1}\|^2 \right]  
 \leq \kappa^2(E_{t-1} + F_{t-1}) \leq \frac{B^2}{2^{2t}}.
\end{align*}

label: eq:error-to-final-min-vi
title: Proof
body_md:
Using the fact that $\widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}$ is $L$-Lipschitz and property \ref{prop:p1-vi}, we have 
\begin{align}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(\bar{z}_T) - \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(z_{T}^*) \right] 
    &\leq  L\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_T - z_{T}^*\right\| \right] \nonumber \\
    &\leq \frac{BL}{2^T}
    \leq B^2\lambda. \label{eq:error-to-final-min-vi}
\end{align}
Note that because the above is a statement with respect to the unregularized gap function, we do not have to worry about whether or not the regularization term is smooth.

What remains is showing $\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(z_{T}^*) \right]=O(\log(n)B^2\lambda)$.  
By the definition of $G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(T)}$ we have 
         \vfill    
\begin{align*}
    G_{\mathcal{D}}(z)
    &= G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(T)}(z) - 2\lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t+1}\rho(z - \bar{z}_t) 
\end{align*}
         \vfill \noindent    
Let $z' = \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{z'\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}}\left\{{\left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}(z'),z_T^*-z' \right\rangle}\right\}$. 
We obtain the following bound on the $ \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(w^*_T,\theta^*_T)$. 
         \vfill    
\begin{align*}
   \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(z^*_T) 
   &=
   \left\langle G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(T)}(z'),z^*_T - z' \right\rangle 
   + \left\langle 2\lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t+1}\rho(z' -\bar{z}_t), z' - z^*_T \right\rangle \\
   &\overset{(i)}\leq
   \left\langle 2\lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t+1}\rho(z' -\bar{z}_t), z' - z^*_T \right\rangle \\
   &\overset{(ii)}{\leq} \left\langle 2\lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t+1}\rho(z_{T}^* - \bar{z}_t),z^*_T - z' \right\rangle \\
   &\overset{(iii)}{\leq} 2B \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t+1}\|\rho(z_{T}^* - \bar{z}_t)\|_* \\
   &\overset{(iv)}{\leq} 2B \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t+1}\left\|z_{T}^* - \bar{z}_t\right\|.
\end{align*}
         \vfill \noindent    
Above, $(i)$ comes from the fact that $z_T^*$ is the equilibrium point of $G_{\mathcal{D}}^{(T)}$. Inequality $(ii)$ uses monotonicity of $\rho$, i.e. $0 \leq \left\langle \rho(z_T^*-\bar{z}_T)-\rho(z'-\bar{z}_T),z_T^*-z' \right\rangle$. Inequality $(iii)$ comes from Holder's inequality and a triangle inequality. Finally, $(iv)$ comes from Assumption \ref{assm:operator}.

Taking the expectation on both sides of the above we have the following derivation,
\begin{align}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \widehat{\operatorname{VI-Gap}}(z_{T}^*) \right] 
    &\leq 2B\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t+1}\left\|z_{T}^* - \bar{z}_t\right\| \right] \nonumber \\
    &\overset{(i)}{\leq} 4B\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t} \left({\left\|z_{t}^* - \bar{z}_t\right\| + \sum\limits_{r=t}^{T-1}\left\|z_{r+1}^*  - z_{r}^*\right\|}\right) \right] \nonumber \\
    &= 4B\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t} \left\|z_{t}^* - \bar{z}_t\right\| + \lambda\sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t}\sum\limits_{r=t}^{T-1} \left\|z_{r+1}^*  - z_{r}^*\right\| \right] \nonumber \\
    &\overset{(ii)}{=} 4B\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t} \left\|z_{t}^* - \bar{z}_t\right\| + \lambda\sum\limits_{r=0}^{T-1}\sum\limits_{t=0}^{r-1} 2^{t} \left\|z_{r+1}^*  - z_{r}^*\right\| \right] \nonumber \\
    &= 4B\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t} \left\|z_{t}^* - \bar{z}_t\right\| + \lambda\sum\limits_{r=0}^{T-1}\left\|z_{r+1}^*  - z_{r}^*\right\|\sum\limits_{t=0}^{r-1} 2^{t} \right] \nonumber \\
    &\overset{(iii)}{\leq} 4B\left({\lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t}\left({\frac{B}{2^{t}}}\right) + \lambda\sum\limits_{r=1}^{T-1}\left({\frac{B
    }{2^{r}}}\right)\sum\limits_{t=0}^{r-1} 2^{t}}\right) \nonumber \\
    &\leq 4B\left({ \lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} 2^{t}\left({\frac{B}{2^{t}}}\right) + \lambda\sum\limits_{r=1}^{T-1}\left({\frac{B}{2^{r-1}}  }\right)\cdot (2^{r}-1)}\right) \nonumber \\
    &= 4\lambda \sum\limits_{t=0}^{T-1} B^2 + 8\lambda\sum\limits_{r=1}^{T-1} B^2 \nonumber \\
    &\leq 12T \lambda B^2 
    \label{eq:final-gap-bound-vi}
\end{align} 
Above, $(i)$ and the following inequality both come from the triangle inequality. Equality $(ii)$ is obtained by rearranging the sums. Inequality $(iii)$  
comes from applying properties \ref{prop:p1-vi} and \ref{prop:p2-vi} proved above. The last equality comes from the setting of $\lambda$ and $T$.

Now using this result in conjunction with Eqn. \eqref{eq:error-to-final-min-vi} 
we have
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{VI-Gap}(\mathcal{R}_{\text{SVI}}) = \sqrt{2}\lambdaB^2 + 12T\lambdaB^2 = O\left({\log(n)B^2\lambda}\right).
\end{align*}
Above we use the fact that $T=\log(\frac{L}{B\lambda})$ and $\lambda \geq \frac{L}{B\sqrt{n'}}$, and thus $T=O(\log(n))$.

title: Proof
body_md:
First, observe that under the setting of $\lambda=\frac{48}{B}\left({\hat{\alpha}\kappa^3 + \frac{\tilde{L}\kappa^2}{\sqrt{n'}}}\right)$ used in the theorem statement that $\log(n)B^2\lambda = O\left({\log(n)B\hat{\alpha}\kappa^3 + \frac{\log^{3/2}(n)B\tilde{L}\kappa^2}{\sqrt{n}}}\right)$. Thus what remains is to show that the distance condition required by Theorem \ref{thm:vi-generalized-rr-convergence} holds. That is, we now show that if $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{sub}}$ satisfies $\hat{\alpha}$-relative stationarity, then 
for all $t\in [T]$ it holds that $\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z^*_{S,t}\right\|^2 \right] \leq \frac{B^2}{12\cdot2^{2t}\kappa^2}$.

To prove this property, we must leverage the induction argument made by Lemma \ref{lem:phase-distance-bound-vi}. Specifically, to prove the condition holds for some $t\in[T]$, assume 
$B_t^2 = \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|z_{t}^* - z^*_{t-1}]\right\| \right]^2 \leq \frac{B^2}{2^{2(t-1)}}$ (recall the base case for $t=1$ trivially holds). As shown in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:phase-distance-bound-vi}, this implies that the quantities
$E_t,F_t$ (as defined in \ref{eq:EF-vi}) are bounded by $\frac{B^2}{2304 \cdot 2^{2t}}$. We thus have
\begin{align} \label{eq:Et-bound-relative-acc-vi}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z^*_{S,t}\right\|^2 \right]
    &\overset{(i)}{\leq} \frac{\kappa\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\langle G_S^{(t)}(\bar{z}_t),\bar{z}_t - z^*_{S,t} \right\rangle \right]}{2^{t}\lambda} 
    \overset{(ii)}{\leq} \frac{2\kappa\hat{\alpha}B}{2^{2t}\lambda} 
    \overset{(iii)}{\leq} \frac{B^2}{12 \cdot 2^{2t}\kappa^2},
\end{align}
where $B_t$ is as defined in property \ref{prop:p2-vi}.
Inequality $(i)$ comes from the strong monotonicity of $G_S^{(t)}$, Fact \ref{fact:rel-acc-bounds-distance-vi}.
Inequality $(iii)$ comes from the setting $\lambda \geq 48\hat{\alpha}\kappa/B$.
Inequality $(ii)$ comes from the $\hat{\alpha}$-relative stationarity assumption on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{sub}}$, which holds so long as the expected distance is sufficiently bounded and the operator is bounded. In this regard, note that
\begin{align*}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|z^*_{S,t}-\bar{z}_{t-1}\| \right] &\leq  \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|z^*_{S,t}-z^*_t\|+\|z^*_t-z^*_{t-1}\|+\|z^*_{t-1}-\bar{z}_{t-1}\| \right] \\
    &\leq (\sqrt{F_t}+B_t+\sqrt{E_{t-1}}+\sqrt{F_{t-1}}) \leq \frac{2B}{2^t}.
\end{align*}
Further, each $g^{(t)}$ is $5L$-bounded. That is, observe 
\begin{align*}    \max\limits_{z\in\ensuremath{\mathcal{Z}}}\|g^{(t)}(z,x)\|_* 
\leq \|z\|_* + \sum_{k=0}^{t-1}2^{k+1}\lambda\|\rho(z-\bar{z}_t)\|_* 
 \leq L + \sum_{k=0}^{t-1}B 2^{k+1}\lambda\leq L + 4B 2^{T}\lambda \leq 5L.
\end{align*}

title: Proof
body_md:
\textit{Privacy Guarantee} We show that $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{sub}}$ is $(\epsilon,\delta)$ at any iteration $t\in[T]$ using the stability properties of the regularized operator. Specifically, the exact equilibrium to $G^{t}_S$. Now because $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{sub}}$ guarantees $\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\hat{z}-z_{S,t}^*\|_2 \right] \leq (\frac{\deltaL}{52^t\lambda n'})$, an application of Markov's inequality implies that with probability at least $1-\delta$ that $\|\hat{z}_t-z_{S,t}^*\|_2 = \left({\frac{1}{\delta}\left({cB e^{-K}}\right)}\right) \leq \frac{L}{2^T\lambda n}$. Thus by a triangle inequality $\hat{z}_t$ is $(\frac{2L}{2^t\lambda n'})$-stable with probability at least $1-\delta$. The guarantees of the Gaussian mechanism thus imply $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{sub}}$ is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-DP.

\textit{Utility Guarantee:} We prove the utility guarantee by leveraging Theorem \ref{thm:vi-generalized-rr-convergence}, which guarantees $\operatorname{VI-Gap}(\mathcal{R})=O(\log(n)B^2\lambda)=O\left({\frac{\log^{3/2}(n)BL}{\sqrt{n}} + \frac{\log^2(n)BL\sqrt{d\log(1/\delta)}}{n\epsilon}}\right)$, so long as for every $t\in[T]$ it holds that
$\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\bar{z}_t - z_{S,t}^* \right]\|_2^2 \leq \frac{B^2}{12\cdot 2^{2t}}$. Note here that under the choice of $\rho$ in Eqn. \eqref{eq:rho-choice}, we satisfy Assuption \ref{assm:operator} with $\kappa=1$. We thus finish the proof with the following analysis,
\begin{align*}
    \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \left\|\bar{z}_t - z_{S,t}^*\right\|_2^2 \right] 
    &= \underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\xi_t\|_2^2 + \|\hat{z}_t - z_{S,t}^*\|_2^2 \right] \\
    &\leq d\sigma_t^2 + \left({\frac{\delta}{5}\cdot\frac{L}{2^t \lambda n'}}\right)^2 \\
    &\leq \frac{64 d L^2\log(2/\delta)}{2^{2t}\lambda^2(n')^2\epsilon^2} + \frac{B^2}{25 \cdot 2^{2t}} 
    \leq \frac{B^2}{12 \cdot 2^{2t}}.
\end{align*}

\textit{Running Time:}
By the guarantees of Lemma \ref{lem:accel-alg-guarantee}, we can achieve the condition 
$\underset{}{\mathbb{E}}\left[ \|\hat{z}-z_{S,t}^*\|_2 \right] \leq (\frac{\deltaL}{52^t\lambda n'})$
made in the description of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathsf{sub}}$ by setting $K = \log\big(\frac{cB}{\delta} \cdot \frac{2^T\lambda n}{L}\big)$. Recall $T=\log_2(\frac{L}{\kappa B\lambda})\leq n$. Thus the overall running time is $O(n + \frac{\beta}{\mu}K\sqrt{n})=O(n + \beta n\log(n/\delta))$.

body_md: Let $f(z;x)=\left\langle z,x \right\rangle$ and define the operator $g(z;x)=\nabla f(z;x) = x$. That is, the strong VI-gap w.r.t. $g$ is equal to the excess population risk w.r.t. the $f$.
